method: Backing is cut larger than the quilt top and is often pieced from standard-width fabric. The calculator adds the entered margin to all four sides of the top, so a 60 x 72 in top with a 4 in margin needs a 68 x 80 in cut. It then costs both layouts: n lengthwise panels, each usable-width wide and the full cut length long, joined along their long edges, and m crosswise strips, each the full cut width long and usable-width tall, joined across. With a seam allowance s, n pieces of usable width w cover n*w - (n-1)*s, so n is the smallest count that reaches the needed span; each layout's yardage is its piece count times the length cut from the bolt divided by 36. The layout with the smaller yardage is recommended, ties going to lengthwise panels, and the buy amount is rounded up to the next 1/8 yard. Batting is reported at the same cut size as the backing. Directional prints that cannot be rotated, long-arm frame requirements, and fabric shrinkage are not modelled. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Quilt finishing guides recommend cutting backing 3-4 in larger than the quilt top on each side
Backing yardage = pieces x cut length / 36; joined span = n x usable width - (n - 1) x seam allowance
